messages:
mike: quick heads-up — after the kernel swap to the new fused-attn on worker-7 we started seeing a subtle drop in decode batching efficiency when tool/function calls pause the decode for structured output. numbers: p50 decode latency +18%, tail tokens per batch down ~22%.
perf-bot: snapshot uploaded https://perf.example.com/2007654321 flamegraph + trace. shows repeated kernel rebinds during paused batches.
ana: is this only when the toolcall emits an explicit stop token, or any tool pause? I remember a case where stop-token vs tool-return timing matters.
li: repro in canary: if tool pause > ~90ms we fragment the current decode batch into many small batches because token_budget_target was hitting a per-request cap and queue policy immediately started a split.
sam: TL;DR: split happens because the scheduler prefers not to hold a batch past the token_budget_target for fairness, but toolcalls cause the active fnframe to stall and the KV cache gets evicted on kernel swap, causing extra work after resume.
mike: exact. profiler shows kernel selection thrash: when a paused batch holds a pinned KV page, the kernel chooser attempts to free memory by swapping kernels, causing context load on resume.
perf-bot: top diff: kernel_swap_count +7x during stalled decodes; KV reload time contributes ~40% of resume latency.
ana: hypothesis: two levers: (1) soften batch formation (hold-window longer for in-flight toolcall), (2) prefer kernel pinning for active fnframes to avoid evictions during short pauses.
li: also could tweak queue policy: give paused fnframes a soft-queue-priority so they don't get preempted out of batching hotspots. e.g., prefer grouping by fnframe_id for up to 200ms.
sam: tried a quick canary with hold_window_ms=200 and toolcall_pause_budget_ms=140, token_budget_target bumped to 96. result: p50 back to baseline, token-per-batch up ~15%.
mike: can you paste the canary config snippet?
li: sure:
```
runtime_config:
  hold_window_ms: 200
  toolcall_pause_budget_ms: 140
  token_budget_target: 96
  prefer_fnframe_grouping: true
  kernel_pin_short_pauses: true
```
ana: nice. any regressions elsewhere? increasing token_budget_target sometimes harms low-latency tiny requests.
sam: measured 95th pct for <=32-token requests: +12ms. but overall cost/unit decreased because fewer KV reloads and fewer tiny batches downstream.
perf-bot: cost model delta: -6.7% tokens/sec equivalent on the canary workload (tool-heavy chat), but small regressive signal on micro-requests.
mike: proposal: rollout staged: enable prefer_fnframe_grouping + kernel_pin_short_pauses only for toolcall-heavy routes (we already signal routes by structured_output=true), keep token_budget_target conservative default and expose override per-route.
ana: agree. implement route tag trigger + observability hook to trigger rollback if p95 latency for non-tool routes rises >8%.
li: I'll open a PR for scheduler changes + kernel pinning flag, and a canary plan. tagging @sam for perf dashboards.
sam: will add dashboard panels: batches_per_second, avg_tokens_per_batch, kernel_swap_rate, kv_reload_ms, p50/p95 decode. Adding alert if kernel_swap_rate increases x3 over baseline.
mike: thanks. quick action items: li PR, sam dashboards, ana canary run, I'll coordinate deploy schedule w/ deploy-bot.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: canary cluster -> worker-7, window 02:00-03:00 UTC. :rocket:
mike: awesome. keep thread if anything weird pops up. :eyes:
